chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu al-Khattab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who enters a thicket and finds an egg of unknown origin, not knowing whether it is from a bird whose meat is disliked or one that is preferred. He said: 'There is a sign in it that does not hide. Look at each egg; if you can distinguish its head from its bottom, then eat it; and if not, leave it.'

key_terms.الْأَجَمَةَ: Thicket or dense bush where birds nest
key_terms.بَيْضًا مُخْتَلِفًا: An egg of unknown origin or type
key_terms.رَأْسَهَا مِنْ أَسْفَلِهَا: Its head from its bottom (tail end)

ai.seo_question: How to determine if a wild egg is halal to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of permissibility) for wild eggs, requiring only a basic morphological check to distinguish the head from the tail. It reflects the practical juristic approach of the Imams, prioritizing ease for the believer by discarding only those eggs where the source animal is unknown or likely haram, thereby avoiding excessive hardship in daily sustenance.
